themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 31 this week—a 313% increase from the 7.5-per-week baseline—suggesting acute pavement deterioration or pothole outbreak in Coney Island/Brighton Beach this week.
evidence: 31 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.5 per-week average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.58)
Concurrent spike in street sign missing complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.4 baseline (z-score: 5.21)
Both spikes suggest infrastructure failure event (weather, maintenance lapse, or construction damage) localized to this district
reporting_angles: On-the-ground photo/video tour of pothole hotspots; compare complaint locations to DOT repair schedules
Interview DOT or CB about what triggered the spike this week—weather event, contractor work, deferred maintenance?

themes_detail.label: Animal Carcass & Park Pest Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped 600% (7 last week vs. 1 baseline) and animal-in-park complaints hit 7 this week—a 522% spike—signaling possible wildlife population surge or sanitation failure in public spaces.
evidence: 7 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 per-week average (z-score: 4.63)
7 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 per-week average (z-score: 6.0)
Dual spike suggests either wildlife influx into parks/neighborhoods or failure of animal control response
reporting_angles: Contact Parks, DSNY, and Animal Care & Control for recent incident logs; identify specific parks mentioned in complaints
Interview residents in high-complaint areas about what they're observing; check for food source or habitat changes (trash, construction, climate)

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Infrastructure & Signage
themes_detail.summary: Street sign–missing complaints surged to 4 this week—a 967% increase from 0.4 per-week baseline—pointing to possible vandalism, wind damage, or maintenance neglect affecting wayfinding and safety.
evidence: 4 street sign–missing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 per-week baseline (z-score: 5.21)
Aligns temporally with street condition spike, suggesting coordinated weather event or infrastructure failure
May affect traffic safety and resident navigation
reporting_angles: Map complaint addresses to identify geographic cluster; check weather records for high winds this week
DOT follow-up: which signs are missing and what is the replacement timeline?

themes_detail.label: Sewer/Root/Sidewalk Damage
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints hit 3 two weeks ago—a 1100% spike from 0.2 per-week baseline—indicating subsurface infrastructure stress or tree-root intrusion affecting pedestrian safety.
evidence: 3 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 per-week average (z-score: 6.35)
Concurrent with tree damage spike (700% increase 3 weeks ago), suggesting storm damage or aging tree canopy root system
Poses trip/fall hazard and potential water intrusion risks
reporting_angles: DEP or Parks investigation: are tree roots intrruding into sewer lines? Are there recent water mains breaks in the area?
Resident safety angle: interview people in affected blocks about trip hazards and flooding

themes_detail.label: Dumpster & Unsanitary Conditions Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints jumped to 3 last week—a 1100% increase from 0.2 per-week baseline—alongside sustained high volume of heat/hot water (1124 total) and unsanitary condition complaints (253 total), suggesting trash management and building maintenance failures.
evidence: 3 dumpster complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 per-week baseline (z-score: 6.35)
Heat/hot water complaints (1124 over 90 days) remain the #2 complaint category, signaling building maintenance crisis
Unsanitary conditions (253 total) suggest broader sanitation and property upkeep issues across district
reporting_angles: DSNY inspection data: are there problem buildings or blocks with repeat dumpster violations?
HPD heat enforcement: which buildings are persistently failing to provide adequate heat/hot water, and why?
